title: Elastic reservation and surge mitigation for Dedicated capacity
creator: Anita Kapoor
description: High-level PRD for introducing an elastic reservation system and surge mitigation controls for Redwood Dedicated. This feature combines soft-reserve tokens, predictive smoothing, and isolation fences to reduce tail latency and tenant interference during transient spikes while preserving reserved guarantees and predictable economics.
problem_statement: Customers with reserved Dedicated capacity experience degraded SLAs during short-duration surges caused by noisy tenants or sudden burst traffic. Current strategies either (a) strictly enforce reservations and block bursts (hurting developer UX) or (b) allow uncontrolled borrowing (hurting isolation and predictability). We need a way to permit safe, observable short bursts while preserving isolation, predictable billing, and graceful preemption when capacity converges.
goals: Allow short-duration bursts beyond tenant reservation with configurable safety windows
Provide predictable eviction/preemption semantics when capacity pressure requires it
Reduce 99th/99.9th percentile latency violations for reserved customers by 30% on typical surge patterns
Give operators visibility and controls to tune elasticity without risking hard SLA breaches
Integrate with rollout/console for per-tenant policy configuration and audit logs
non_goals: Replace long-term autoscale commitments or reserved billing models
Provide per-request QoS beyond existing request routing primitives (this focuses on capacity-level policies)
Custom billing reconciliation flows beyond tagging and usage export (billing is separate)
user_stories: As an SRE for a large customer, I want their reserved pool to tolerate short bursts without manual intervention so customer-facing features remain responsive.
As a platform operator, I want a safety budget that tenants can borrow from under light load and a clear fallback path when pressure rises so we can balance utilization and SLAs.
As a product manager, I want a dashboard showing borrowed capacity, preemption events, and per-tenant surge trends so I can reason about policy changes.
As a tenant admin, I want a configurable burst tolerance and preemption priority so my critical routes are less likely to be evicted during capacity pressure.
functional_requirements: Introduce a 'soft-reserve' token pool per tenant: an ephemeral allowance that can be consumed when reserved allocation is saturated
Soft-reserve tokens expire after a configurable TTL (default 60s); consumption must be tracked in the console and exported to metrics
Predictive smoothing service that uses short-term telemetry (1min, 5min) to pre-warm capacity and adjust soft-reserve budgets automatically
Preemption policy with ordered fallback: (1) revoke soft-reserve tokens, (2) throttle burst requests via 429 or queued retries, (3) route to compatible lower-cost model variant if configured
Per-tenant isolation fence tags to ensure reserved pools cannot be permanently starved by a single noisy sub-tenant
Operator controls in Console: global defaults, per-project overrides, emergency disable toggle, and incident timeline showing preemptions
Audit logs for borrow/grant/preempt events sent to customer audit stream and internal logging sink
API/SDK surfaces: endpoint to query remaining soft-reserve allowance and to subscribe to preemption callbacks for long-lived jobs
Integration with existing autoscale: decouple short-term burst handling from scale-up decisions to avoid unnecessary instance churn
nonfunctional_requirements: Soft-reserve accounting must be accurate within 1% over 5m window
Preemption decision latency must be <200ms from detection to enforcement
Telemetry and metrics for borrowed capacity must be emitted with <30s delay to Console
Feature rollout must support per-region enablement and gradual ramp to 100% to avoid global regressions
Performance overhead of predictive smoothing service should not increase p99 latency by more than 5% on baseline workloads
acceptance_criteria: Create and consume soft-reserve tokens in a non-prod Dedicated cluster and observe borrow/return lifecycle in Console
Simulate a noisy-tenant surge: other tenants' reserved pools should not drop below guaranteed allocations after soft-reserve exhaustion and preemption sequence completes
Metrics demonstrate at least 20% reduction in p99 latency violations in synthetic surge tests compared to baseline without elastic reserve
Preemption events are recorded in audit logs with tenant ID, reason, and timestamp and are exportable via the existing audit API
API endpoint returns soft-reserve allowance and is present in SDK with basic unit tests
Operator feature flags and per-tenant overrides are working and respected during a gradual rollout
Security review completed and no critical findings remain (if security_review_required=true)
success_metrics: Percent reduction in p99 latency violations for reserved customers during surges: target >= 30%
Mean time to preemption enforcement under pressure: <200ms
Operator MTTR for burst incidents reduced by 40% due to better observability
Utilization uplift of Dedicated fleets during normal periods: +5-10% without increased violation rates
Number of billing disputes related to unexpected evictions: reduced to near-zero for cohorts using default policies
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: (1) Internal canary on staging Dedicated clusters with synthetic surges, (2) Small beta with 5% of production tenants in a single region with opt-in, (3) Expand to 25% production tenants across two regions, (4) Full region enablement with adjustable defaults. Each stage includes load tests, security sign-off, and a 48-hour observation window before widening.
rollout_stages: Canary: staging clusters, internal engineering traffic
General availability: enabled by default with operator dashboard
dependencies: ENG-3399 (console feature gates and operator controls)
ENG-4021 (preemption enforcement hooks in serving runtime)
SEC-88 (security review for audit export changes)
risks: Incorrect accounting could allow steal of reserved capacity causing SLA breaches
Predictive smoothing may over-provision and increase costs if model is not tuned
Complexity in policy interactions can create surprising eviction behavior for customers
Telemetry lag may hide pressure leading to delayed preemption and transient violations
mitigations: Start with conservative defaults (small soft-reserve budgets, short TTLs) and observe
Implement guardrail checks in runtime that never allow guaranteed reservation to be reduced below contract limits
Provide clear operator runbooks and buyback controls to rollback policy changes quickly
Expose detailed metrics and alerts for any discrepancy between reserved usage and accounting
open_questions: Should soft-reserve consumption be billable or merely a tracked metric for invoicing follow-up?
What default TTL and budget sizing heuristics work best across our customers (per-tenant vs. per-project)?
How do we present preemption priority to customers in a way that is actionable but not confusing?
Do we need a marketplace-style toggle for tenants to purchase guaranteed burst escrow for critical workloads?
